what_its_for: Maraviroc is an antiviral medicine used to treat HIV (the virus that causes AIDS) in adults and children who weigh at least 10 kg (about 22 pounds). It works by blocking the doorway (called CCR5) that a certain type of HIV uses to enter your immune cells. This helps lower the amount of HIV in your blood and keeps your immune system stronger. It is always used together with other HIV medicines, never alone.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take maraviroc with or without food — it does not matter. Try to take it at the same times every day to keep the medicine working as well as possible. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is okay. If you have trouble swallowing tablets, ask your pharmacist about the liquid form (oral solution). Always take maraviroc exactly as your doctor prescribed and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is 150 mg, 300 mg, or 600 mg taken TWICE a day (every 12 hours), depending on the other HIV medicines you are taking. Your doctor will choose the right dose for you based on your full medication list. For children, the dose is based on weight and is calculated by your doctor or pharmacist. Never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. If your next dose is due within 6 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Skipping doses or stopping the medicine can allow HIV to multiply and become harder to treat.
storage: Store maraviroc tablets at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Store it away from heat, light, and moisture — do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If you have the liquid oral solution, check the package label for specific storage instructions, as it may need to be stored differently.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement) while on maraviroc — it can lower the amount of maraviroc in your blood and make it stop working. Tell ALL your doctors, dentists, and pharmacists about every medicine, vitamin, and supplement you take, because many drugs can interact with maraviroc. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice in large amounts, as it may affect how the medicine works. Do not share needles, syringes, or personal items like razors or toothbrushes, as HIV can still be spread to others even while you are on treatment. Always use a condom during sexual activity to help prevent spreading HIV to others.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you notice: signs of a serious liver problem such as yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe stomach pain, or unusual tiredness; signs of a serious allergic skin reaction such as a rash with blisters, peeling skin, sores in your mouth, or fever; signs of a heart problem such as chest pain, fast or uneven heartbeat, or feeling faint; signs of a severe allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; signs of infection (fever, chills, severe sore throat) or any new or worsening symptoms after starting treatment. Also tell your doctor if you feel dizzy when standing up, as maraviroc can lower blood pressure.
when_it_works: Maraviroc starts working right away to help block HIV from entering your cells. However, you will not feel any immediate difference. Your doctor will check blood tests called viral load (the amount of HIV in your blood) and CD4 count (a measure of immune strength) regularly — usually every 3 to 6 months — to see how well the medicine is working. It may take several weeks to months to see meaningful improvement in your lab results. It is very important to keep taking all your HIV medicines every day as directed, even if you feel fine, to keep the virus under control.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, your doctor may need to adjust your dose — make sure your doctor knows about any kidney issues. Liver problems: Maraviroc is processed by the liver; use with caution if you have liver disease or hepatitis B or C. Pregnant or breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding is generally not recommended for people living with HIV in places where safe formula is available, to prevent passing HIV to the baby. Children: Maraviroc can be used in children weighing at least 10 kg (22 lbs); the dose will be carefully calculated by your doctor. Older adults: Use with care, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness and low blood pressure.
